guided.title: Does soil moisture follow the rain?
guided.question: In the Santiago region, do wet and dry years show up in the soil?
guided.lesson: Yes, strongly, year to year — but GLDAS is driven by observed rain, so part of this agreement is built into the model.

guided.title: Where evapotranspiration depends on rain
guided.question: In Valparaíso, do years with more rain also return more water to the air?
guided.lesson: In the dry centre and north, yes. Switch the region to Los Ríos: there the link disappears, consistent with a place where water is plentiful and energy, not rain, limits evaporation (an interpretation, not tested).

guided.title: Warm years, less snow?
guided.question: In O'Higgins, do warmer years have less Andean snow?
guided.lesson: The sign is negative in most central regions, but after correcting for 64 associations none is clearly distinguishable from chance except Los Lagos. A plausible idea that this data cannot yet confirm.
